QuestionStmt.S: A liquid drop having surface energy $E$ is spread into 729 droplets of same size. The final surface energy of the droplets is

Solution.S:
Let the radius of the big drop be $R$ and the radius of each small droplet be $r$.

Initial surface energy:

$$E = 4\pi R^2 T$$

Volume conservation:

$$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 729 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$$

$$R^3 = 729 r^3$$

$$R = 9r \quad \Rightarrow \quad r = \frac{R}{9}$$

Final total surface energy:

$$E_{\text{final}} = 729 \times 4\pi r^2 \times T$$

$$= 4\pi T \times 729 \times \left(\frac{R}{9}\right)^2$$

$$= 4\pi T \times 729 \times \frac{R^2}{81}$$

$$= 4\pi T \times 9 \times R^2$$

$$= 9 \times (4\pi R^2 T)$$

$$= 9E$$

Thus the final surface energy is $9E$, which corresponds to option B.
